findings.evidence: src/banking_tasci/data/annotations.py defines AnnotationRecord with fields record_id, source, region, text, previous_text, context_available, aspects, intent, intent_ambiguous, alternative_intent, annotator_id, annotation_status, notes. findings.recommended_action: Reuse context.py unchanged in the new pipeline; it does not need to be rewritten, only re-pointed at new sampling targets.

findings.evidence: scripts/create_splits.py: DEFAULT_TRAIN_RATIO = 0.70, DEFAULT_VALIDATION_RATIO = 0.15, DEFAULT_TEST_RATIO = 0.15 (lines ~40-42). The module docstring's own usage example explicitly shows --train-ratio 0.70 --validation-ratio 0.15 --test-ratio 0.15. Section 27 explicitly prohibits '70/15/15 splits' as a legacy behaviour. Required ratios are 0.80/0.10/0.10 (Section 15, Section 28 canonical config).

findings.impact: This is a directly, explicitly prohibited legacy default per Section 27. The CLI already accepts --train-ratio/--validation-ratio/--test-ratio as overridable arguments, so correct ratios CAN be supplied today without code changes -- but the stored default is wrong and will silently produce legacy splits if a caller omits the flags.
findings.recommended_action: Do not change create_splits.py's defaults in place yet (it is shared with legacy workflows). findings.evidence: create_splits.py's group_key() correctly groups sentence-level review records back to their parent review via source_record_id (set by context.py's build_review_sentence_records()), falling back to record_id for ungrouped records (e.g. tweets). assign_groups_to_splits() is a pure, seeded, deterministic function (verified by reading the full implementation: uses only a locally-constructed random.Random(seed), never global RNG state) that assigns WHOLE groups to a single split using largest-remainder stratified allocation by intent. An optional --near-dup-csv flag further merges near-duplicate groups via near_dup_group_id so near-duplicates never cross split boundaries. Section 23.2's hard precondition (refuse to run on any invalid record, write no manifest) is implemented in main() before any grouping occurs.
findings.impact: No gap in the group-aware leakage MECHANISM itself. This is some of the strongest, most reusable code in the repository.
findings.recommended_action: Reuse this splitter's grouping/allocation logic unchanged; only the default ratios (R21) and the leakage-grouping KEYS need extending once duplicate_group/leakage_group/thread_id/conversation_id fields exist in the new schema (R13).

findings.evidence: create_splits.py currently writes train_manifest.csv/validation_manifest.csv/test_manifest.csv (record_id-only CSVs) and split_report.json. findings.evidence: src/banking_tasci/data/clean.py:_shingle used Python's builtin hash() on shingle strings. Python randomises string hashing per process via PYTHONHASHSEED, so MinHash signatures - and therefore near-duplicate grouping - differed between runs on identical input. Demonstrated: tests/test_near_duplicates.py::test_detect_near_identical_texts_flagged passed and failed across identical consecutive invocations (pass/fail/fail/pass); with PYTHONHASHSEED pinned it passed 4/4. Replaced with _stable_hash (blake2b, 8-byte digest): 6/6 stable unpinned, and 166 related tests pass across clean/near-duplicate/ingest/resampling modules.
findings.impact: Near-duplicate detection was non-reproducible despite its docstring promising determinism for a given cfg.seed. This affects leakage prevention, which depends on stable duplicate grouping - a correctness issue for Requirements 15.2, not merely a flaky test. It was masked by luck in earlier runs rather than introduced by this session.
findings.recommended_action: Closed. Guarded by ::test_shingle_hashing_is_process_independent, ::test_near_duplicate_detection_is_deterministic_across_processes (both across four PYTHONHASHSEED values), and ::test_clean_module_does_not_use_builtin_hash_for_shingles. Previously-computed near_dup_group_id values in existing artifacts were produced with the old unstable hash and should be regarded as non-reproducible if ever recomputed.

findings.evidence: src/banking_tasci/data/sa_candidate_filter.py (920 lines) contains DUPLICATE definitions: CandidateResult at lines 189 and 748, classify_candidate at 198 and 757, is_potential_zero_aspect at 313 and 892, and _any at 353 and 375. The later definitions shadow the earlier ones, so the LIVE classify_candidate is the regex variant at line 757 (confirmed via inspect.getsourcelines). This is the same defect class as R41. Critically, the live row-wise classify_candidate DISAGREES with the vectorised keyword logic that produced the authoritative 100,768 count: measured on a 40,000-row sample of the real parent source, 1,838 vectorised candidates versus 2,592 row-wise candidates - 756 disagreements (1.89%), with the row-wise path more permissive. The September 2026 run log records 'Applying evidence-based candidate filter (vectorised keyword matching)', confirming the vectorised path is authoritative.
findings.impact: Had the materialisation naively 'imported one canonical filtering function' as classify_candidate, it would have selected a DIFFERENT record set and failed to reproduce 100,768 - silently producing a wrong corpus had the count assertion not caught it.
findings.recommended_action: Mitigated, not yet fully resolved. The authoritative vectorised logic was extracted verbatim into the new src/banking_tasci/data/sa_candidates_v2.py, which is now the single canonical selection used by materialisation, tests, and documentation; it reproduces 100,768 and the full rule breakdown exactly. sa_candidate_filter.py itself was deliberately NOT modified this session because scripts/resample_south_africa_v2.py and the legacy tests depend on its current behaviour and its completed outputs are preserved. Remaining work: de-duplicate that module behind a compatibility plan, and reconcile or deprecate the divergent row-wise classify_candidate.

findings.evidence: src/banking_tasci/data/south_africa_sampler.py's _prepare() built the _group column via DataFrame.apply(_group_key, axis=1). Over the full 100,768-row real corpus this coerced the (almost entirely None) result column so every missing group collapsed onto the same shared float('nan') object. The selection loop's conflict check (group is not None and group in used_groups) treated NaN as 'not None', so after the first ungrouped record was accepted into used_groups, every later ungrouped record in the same length band looked like a duplicate-group conflict by object identity. Measured before the fix: sample_south_africa(REAL_CORPUS, seed=42) selected only 12 of 500 target records, with duplicate_group_conflicts=201512 against only 24 genuine near-duplicate groups in the whole corpus. Did not reproduce on the ~1,500-row synthetic test fixtures used elsewhere in the suite, which is why it was not caught earlier.
findings.impact: This was a silent, severe under-selection bug in the only sampler that supplies the 500-record South African half of the gold corpus. Left unfixed, any real (non-dry-run) gold write would have produced a 12-record, heavily-skewed-by-bank selection instead of 500/100-per-bank, while still reporting it as the result of a seed-42 deterministic run.
findings.recommended_action: Closed. Added _is_missing_group() (treats None and float NaN as 'no group') and used it at the column-normalisation step and all three group-conflict comparison sites. Re-verified against the real materialised corpus: exactly 500 selected, 100 per bank, 0 shortages, 0 duplicate_group_conflicts. make test re-run clean at 916 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped.
